subject: Clarify billing for streaming partial responses and reconnects
messages:
From: Lucas Hargreaves <lucas.h@techwave.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Question on streaming billing — partial generations and reconnects

Hi Sean,

We're getting ready for a 6-week pilot and have a practical question about how streaming responses are billed. Our app makes frequent short streaming requests (partial generations) and sometimes the client disconnects and reconnects to resume (we handle retries client-side). In pilot runs we've seen a few dozen reconnects per hour per user.

Specific questions:
- If a stream sends 40 tokens and then the client disconnects and reconnects to request the continuation, do we get billed for both segments (i.e., 40 then 60) or only final output?
- How are retries handled when the client requests the same tail of the generation (duplicate tokens) — are duplicates deduplicated for billing?
- If a connection drops and Redwood returns a partial chunk, do you bill for the partial chunk even when we request a new generation?

We want to understand baseline hosted API charges so we can model pilot costs. Also, procurement will ask for a line in the SOW clarifying retry/stream billing. Can you share the authoritative wording we can put in the SOW?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Lucas
Head of Integrations, TechWave
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Hargreaves <lucas.h@techwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing — partial generations and reconnects

Hi Lucas — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: we bill tokens generated and delivered by the model; streaming breaks do not automatically cause duplicate billing in most reconnection patterns, but there are edge cases. I looped in Neha (account lead) and Olga (SE) to give the precise wording you can include in the SOW and an example cost calculation for your pilot.

Proposed next steps:
- Olga will outline the exact billing rules and examples (we'll attach a one-page rate-card note).
- We'll propose a small pilot credit to cover expected retry noise and keep your trial predictable.
- If helpful, we'll schedule a 30-min call and include logs from a sample session.

Thanks — will be quick to resolve.

— Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Hargreaves <lucas.h@techwave.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing — partial generations and reconnects

Hi Lucas,

Thanks for the detailed scenario — here is the authoritative behavior for hosted streaming billing on Redwood:

1) Billing unit: tokens generated by the model that are transmitted to the client (we charge per-token generated, see attached rate note).

2) Partial chunks and disconnects: every token that the model outputs and we successfully stream to the client counts toward billing, even if the client disconnects immediately after receiving that chunk.

3) Reconnects and resumed generations: if the client reconnects and requests a continuation using the exact model state (same conversation ID and KV cache resumption) we avoid re-generating already-output tokens. In practice this requires using our resume token API or passing the last known server-side cursor. If the client simply issues a brand-new generation request that reproduces prior tokens, that re-generation is billed as new tokens.

4) Retries and duplicates: we do not perform automatic cross-request deduplication. Deduplication is possible if the client uses the resume endpoint/key so the backend can leverage the server-side KV cache; otherwise duplicate tokens are billable.

5) Grace period for aborted streams: for small aborted streams triggered by network flakiness (<500ms between last ack and disconnect) our runtime can often stitch sessions and avoid re-generation, but this is not guaranteed and should not be relied on for cost modeling.

Example (your numbers):
- Client A: stream sends 40 tokens then disconnects; client reconnects and resumes correctly via resume token -> billed: 40 + 60 = 100 tokens (no duplicate billing)
- If client reconnects but issues a fresh request that reproduces the first 40 tokens -> billed: 40 + 40 + 60 = 140 tokens (duplicates billed)

Attached: streaming-ratecard-clarity.pdf (concise billing language for SOW and a sample pilot cost table).

Recommended SOW clause (plain text you can copy):
"Redwood will bill for tokens generated and transmitted by the model during the hosted streaming session. Tokens that are re-generated due to client-initiated fresh requests (i.e., not using Redwood's resume mechanism) are billable as separate generation tokens. For transient network failures, Redwood's runtime will attempt to stitch sessions where feasible; such stitching is not guaranteed and customers should use the resume API to avoid duplicate charges."

If you'd like, we can provide a short sample integration showing the resume token flow (node/python snippets).

Cheers,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: streaming-ratecard-clarity.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
From: Lucas Hargreaves <lucas.h@techwave.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@techwave.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:55:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing — partial generations and reconnects

Thanks Olga — that's very helpful and clear. Couple of follow-ups:

1) For our pilot we're estimating ~1.2M tokens/day across 300 active seats and expect ~0.8% reconnection/retry noise from mobile clients. That delta materially affects our pilot budget. Can Redwood provide a small pilot credit to cover estimated retry-related overages?

2) Procurement asks for the exact SOW wording to counter-review. Can you provide the wording as a short PDF (we can attach to the SOW) and confirm if Redwood will agree to a one-off clause that we won't be retro-billed for duplicate tokens that are demonstrably caused by a known Redwood server issue?

We're ready to sign the pilot contract once we have those points clarified.

Best,
Lucas
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Hargreaves <lucas.h@techwave.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Feb 2026 15:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on streaming billing — partial generations and reconnects

Hi Lucas — appreciate the quick turnaround. We can do the following to keep the pilot moving:

- Pilot credit: Redwood will provide a one-time pilot credit equal to 20% of the estimated token spend to cover retry/connect noise. We'll include this as a credit line in the pilot invoice. (Attachment: pilot-credit-proposal.xlsx)
- SOW wording: we'll produce a short PDF that includes Olga's recommended clause plus an explicit carve-out: "Redwood will not retro-bill for duplicate tokens if Redwood investigation determines the duplicate generation was caused by Redwood infrastructure malfunction." That carve-out requires mutually agreed incident evidence (logs).
- Next steps: Sean will share the updated SOW PDF and the credit line; procurement can accept the wording or request edits.

Sean — I'll leave it to you to confirm the credit amount in the pilot paperwork and attach the SOW PDF.

Thanks,
Neha
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
